study.question: Observed limitation: g2-r0010-recent10 outperformed equal10 (click AUC .6626241153 vs .6605926365), early10 (.6602366530), and full100 (.6597487028); full history was slower (362.13s vs 309.55s recent). g2-r0011 retained the recent/equal gap with occupied-only scoring (.6624553103 vs .6605188821), so empty-slot Dice contamination does not explain the whole gap. g2-r0012-recent_forward/recent_reverse kept all 30 per-sample stratum counts fixed but changed content placement: .6624553103 vs .6607513788; equal_forward/equal_reverse were .6605188821 vs .6608500755. The partition contrast was .0019364282 for chronological content and -.0000986967 for reversed content (interaction .0020351249). This is one-seed controlled support conditional on the inherited stratum schedule, not repeated support for general recency. Same-seed chronological replays across r0011/r0012 are not independent repetitions. The current module sums all temporal blocks before task readout, so it cannot distinguish two histories with the same target-weighted total but different recent/older allocation. Earlier trajectories constrain the choice: g2-r0000-match20 (.6572579523) did not beat rotated20 (.6575160909) or uniform20 (.6574686669); g2-r0009-target10 (.6598396641) trailed history10 (.6600522423) and its .6606469405 parent; learned within-block target selection is not assumed beneficial. g2-r0008 encode-before/pool-before variants were nearly equal (.6599379026/.6599585643), without improvement over their simpler ancestor. g2-r0005-private_residual raised auxiliary quality at added cost (435.13s, 56.32M parameters), while click .6600991552 trailed its .6606469405 parent; this was private embedding capacity, not the proposed temporal logit readout. Current click improvements have a serious scope limit: baseline-din auxiliary AUCs cart/fav/buy were .849069702/.864897493/.870182275, whereas g2-r0012-recent_forward gives .712407043/.728684509/.671858364. The present study does not claim to fix this gradient-sharing/auxiliary-label limitation. Question: after retaining recent-event resolution, does erasing temporal identity in the final history sum remain a bottleneck for joint context/target/task prediction?
study.hypothesis: Compression resolution and downstream temporal information interact. Fine recent summaries help, but summing them with old summaries erases whether target-relevant information is recent or persistent. A small task-specific nonlinear branch over context, target, total T, and signed contrast C=R-O can condition predictions on recent versus older evidence while reusing the same 30 compressed/scored slots. R sums the last ten exposure positions, O the preceding ninety, separately within the inherited three strata; click reads the uniform stratum and auxiliaries sum the two feedback strata. A collapsed branch receives [context,target,T,T] instead, with identical trainable parameter count and operators, controlling added generic nonlinear capacity. The last-ten boundary is prospective, tied to the existing bin boundary at position90, not optimized on a new validation outcome. It denotes exposure order, not elapsed time. This is a compression/readout co-design hypothesis; separate temporal representations and feature interaction are established ideas, and novelty remains unverified.

inherited_components: Full g2-r0012-recent_forward standalone source as implementation ancestor; equal_forward is the exact matching alternate-layout reference.
DIN-adapted field/action embeddings, unnormalized local scorer, occupied PopulationScorer and four original Dice towers.
Fixed recent widths [20,20,20,20,10,5,2,1,1,1] or equal widths [10]*10, exact stratum counts, all-history click versus feedback-separated auxiliary compression, and chronological identity routing.
Auxiliary-union masks, context-only shared gradient path, blocked scorer/item/action auxiliary paths, functional scorer evaluation and cloned BatchNorm state.
study.proposed_difference: Keep the old logit tower and add one task-specific residual head: Linear(D+V,32), ReLU, Linear(32,1), where D is the inherited context+target+total input width and V is history value width. The extra V input is recent-minus-older C for separate cells, duplicate total T for collapsed cells. Compute total and contrast in all cells; expose the contrast only at readout, without changing assignments, counts, scorer populations or raw input. No age IDs, elapsed times, current labels, extra event fields, new losses, private embeddings or extra histories are introduced. Append heads after the original reset_parameters inside torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[]), zero their output weights/biases, and move all modules together. Original logits initially replay the matching ancestor; heads train from scratch. All four cells have exactly the same module graph and parameter dimensions. Added parameters are 4*(32*(D+V+1)+33), expected65796 if D=400,V=112; expected total32126249 and dense333033 versus inherited32060453/dense267237, subject to host measurement. C and T together invertibly recover R/O; collapsed input has lower functional rank despite equal allocated parameters, so the contrast identifies access to temporal information plus its optimization effects, not an abstract parameter-independent theorem. Before any host training, verify finite FP32/BF16 forward and backward for empty/full/partial/holey histories, B=1 evaluation and B>=2 training; all four outputs [B,1] and label-order permutations. Check padded item/action-ID and padded task-mask invariance, target-action exclusion, and exact last-ten versus first-ninety assignment in both partitions. Compare totals and signed contrasts against direct block-wise references, including gradients, and reconstruct R=(T+C)/2, O=(T-C)/2 for every stratum. At fixed weights, separate/collapsed inputs must agree for histories wholly in last ten positions; empty histories must produce zero history features. Verify identical inherited tensors, CPU RNG continuation, embedding aliases, and initial predictions against corresponding recent/equal ancestors; new residual outputs exactly zero initially. Auxiliary-only loss must not update shared scorer/item/action parameters through either old or new path; context and auxiliary residual-head gradients must remain available. Initial hidden-head gradients are zero by design at zero final weights: test source-gradient ownership again after temporarily setting final residual weights to small nonzero values in a disposable check model. Verify only primary scorer buffers persist updates, inference reuses primary strata, and occupied zero/one-row rules. Measure actual parameters, allocated GPU seconds, train/validation/wall time, examples processed, peak memory, throughput and model-batch p50/p95 latency. Local validation performed here: syntax/AST, config/default agreement, source import boundary, unchanged inherited representation/compression/scorer/gating AST, and 120 independent scalar pooling cases; no torch is installed, so tensor prerequisites are unexecuted. The public workspace provides code and committed validation receipts, not raw parquet execution or a callable training/scoring interface. This proposal relies on frozen host readiness receipts; it does not claim to reverify raw digests, loader behavior or tensor execution locally.
predictions: Primary predeclared effect: recent_separate click AUC exceeds recent_collapsed on identical full validation data and frozen recipe; compare Logloss and measured cost rather than claiming efficiency from parameter formulas.

Estimate the readout effect in equal layout too. A positive interaction [(recent_separate-recent_collapsed)-(equal_separate-equal_collapsed)] supports complementary fine resolution and temporal retention. An equal effect in both layouts supports only a general late temporal-readout benefit.

The residual may improve generic context/target interaction in both collapsed and separate models; that benefit alone is not evidence for temporal preservation. Compare collapsed cells to exact occupied recent/equal references and the incumbent/din separately.

Temporal-information benefit should be most plausible in 17-64 and >64 history bins, where both windows can be occupied. At fixed weights, histories entirely within the last10 positions have C=T, so separate/collapsed inputs agree; trained models can still differ through optimization and global shared parameters. Existing 1-16 bin mixes the boundary and is not a clean negative control.

All four task AUC/Logloss values, auxiliary-only mean AUC, counts and the existing empty/1-16/17-64/>64 slices will be reported; any auxiliary loss or AUC regression limits claims of unified four-task improvement.
falsifiers: No positive recent_separate versus recent_collapsed effect, or a gain attributable wholly to collapsed generic added capacity, leaves the proposed temporal bottleneck unsupported for this implementation.

Separate readout gains in equal layout but not recent layout refute the predicted complementarity of recent fine resolution and temporal retention; it may indicate an alternative low-cost replacement rather than the claimed interaction.

Failure of initial-ancestor replay, padding invariance, recent/older reconstruction, gradient ownership, Dice-buffer ownership, output schema or finite BF16 execution invalidates causal interpretation and requires an accounted implementation correction before training.

A single favorable result, unpaired independent seeds, or improvements only in an exploratory slice do not establish repeated mechanism support. If paired repeats reverse the contrasts, downgrade support and retain all outcomes.

Higher quality accompanied by substantially higher measured training/inference cost can remain a quality-cost tradeoff, but cannot establish an efficiency improvement; no unmeasured equal-compute claim is allowed.
alternative_explanations: The signed temporal feature changes numerical conditioning and gradient geometry; equal allocated parameter count does not equate effective feature rank or optimization capacity.
Any gains may come from generic residual context/target/total interactions or scratch optimization trajectories; collapsed heads and zero-output ancestor initialization address only part of this.

The boundary at10 exposures may act as a history-length or feedback-composition signal rather than preference drift; no wall-clock times are available. Fixed weights short-history equality and existing length slices constrain, but do not eliminate, this explanation.
Recent/equal layouts change counts, mean variance and occupied Dice population. Readout pairs hold them exactly fixed; the cross-layout interaction still includes those inherited differences.
Global scorer/tower BatchNorm couples examples during training. Empty-history trained-model differences can arise indirectly and do not prove useful recent-history content.
Auxiliary source detachment and union-mask compression already degrade auxiliary metrics; a favorable click result must not be described as simultaneous four-task improvement.
Repeated validation-guided selection and the single frozen seed can overstate gains. No held-out feedback is available or requested. Paper links/card provenance are not local transfer evidence.
